message.reasoning:
We need to diagnose failure cause based on logs. The result: robot collided 27 times, never reached goal, ended far from start (-8.37,-10.2) after 37s. Path planning succeeded (plan_summary accepted, path 60 points). Choose_command picks many stop, back, turn_r, forward_slow etc. The robot seems to be stuck near start, colliding with arena mover (maybe moving forklift). Collisions start at t=31.433. The choose logs show many map_clearance_object_gap picks leading to back commands, then stop, etc. Likely the lookahead_target is wrong: using _base_loop_forward_target directly, but that function expects path and pose, returns forward point or None. However _base_loop_forward_target also updates path_progress_s etc? Actually _base_loop_forward_target is used inside base loop to compute forward target but also updates path_progress_s? It uses robot = _base_loop_projection(path, pose[:2], _BASE_LOOP_ST["path_progress_s"]). It updates state["path_progress_s"] later in guard target step. In lookahead_target we call it directly, which will also compute forward target but not go through guard. However _base_loop_forward_target returns a point (x,y) but does not respect the target distance constraints? It returns None if remaining < target_min_ahead_m. In our code, if None we fallback to path[-1]. That could cause target far ahead (goal) leading to collision? Actually fallback to last waypoint (goal) which is far away (34m). Then follow_cmd will compute large distance, produce high speed v up to 1.5, w based on bearing error, causing robot to drive straight into obstacles. The base guard later will check target guard: it will compute projected and may reject due to unsafe_connector etc, then fallback to forward target, but our target may be overwritten? Wait flow: In base loop after lookahead_target, they call _base_loop_guard_target(state["path"], pose, target, t). This guard will examine requested target (our target) and possibly replace with forward target if unsafe. So if we gave goal far away, guard will see that target is far beyond max_ahead (2.0m) and reject, then compute forward target via _base_loop_forward_target, which may be None if robot is near start? At early times robot is near start, path_progress_s initially None, so forward_target may be None? Actually _base_loop_forward_target uses projection = None, which computes robot projection using _base_loop_projection(path, pose[:2], _BASE_LOOP_ST["path_progress_s"]). Since path_progress_s is None initially, they use hint_s = None, then compute projection. Then remaining = current["total"] - current["s"]; if remaining < target_min_ahead_m - 1e-12, returns None. At start robot at start, path_progress_s is None, robot projection maybe near start, remaining is total length of path (around 34m). That is > target_min_ahead_m, so forward_target returns a point 0.3-2.0m ahead (the min ahead). So guard will replace target with that forward point. So fallback is okay. However our lookahead_target returns path[-1] only if forward_target returned None. That may happen when robot near goal? But early on it's not None. So maybe not cause.

Another issue: plan_path returns raw_path of cell centers, but does not ensure start and goal within 0.5m of first/last points. In validation, _base_validate_plan will add connectors if start_gap > 0.5? Actually endpoint limit is 0.5m. start_gap_m is distance from path[0] to start_xy. In plan summary start_gap_m 0.112 < 0.5, goal_gap_m 0.111 <0.5, so okay. Path points 60.

Collision count 27 suggests robot collided with moving object (arena mover). Maybe the problem is that lookahead_target returns a tuple (x,y) but base expects (x,y) as point; they then guard target. However our lookahead_target returns target[0], target[1] where target may be a tuple (x,y). That's fine.

But the collisions happen early at t~31s, after many back commands. The robot is moving backwards (v negative) due to chooser picking back candidate when follow command v positive but map stop? Actually chooser picks back when map clearance low. The robot may be stuck near obstacle, map_stop triggers replan after 10s, but path not updated because same path still blocked? The path maybe goes through a narrow corridor that is blocked by moving object (forklift). The robot should replan around moving object, but planner does not consider dynamic objects; only static map. So collisions with moving objects are expected; base expects robot to avoid via chooser (which uses map and object predictions). However chooser may not have sufficient object prediction because our follow_cmd may produce high speed causing collisions before chooser can react. The chooser uses check_motion with horizon 3s and object prediction; but if v is high and robot heading directly towards moving object, check_motion may detect collision and reject, causing chooser to pick stop or back. But logs show many back picks, meaning chooser saw map clearance object gap (map blocked). But collisions still occurred. Perhaps because our follow_cmd returns high speed (up to 1.5) even when distance is large, causing robot to travel fast into moving object before chooser can stop? However chooser runs after follow_cmd, it evaluates candidate follow (v,w) and others. If follow leads to collision, it should choose another safe candidate (stop). In logs, at t=28.5 pick turn_r, then back, forward_slow, etc. At t=31 pick back etc. So chooser is already picking safe candidates (back) but collisions still happen. Maybe collisions are due to our lookahead_target returning a point that is not reachable (segment_free from pose to target fails), causing guard to fallback to forward_target but maybe forward_target is None leading to target = path[-1] (goal) which is far, causing unsafe_connector? Actually guard will reject if unsafe_connector, then fallback to forward_target again; if that also fails, they set target = None and later use robot_path_s point as target (the robot's current projection). In that case follow_cmd receives target maybe same as robot position (distance 0) leading to v=0. But collisions still happen earlier.

Another clue: The choose logs show many picks of back, forward_slow, turn_r with map clearance object gap reason, indicating map clearance (static map) is insufficient, not object. The map is static; why map clearance is low? Possibly because robot is near wall or obstacle; the path goes near walls, and due to our path being cell centers (grid 0.5m), the path may cut corners too close to walls; segment_free checks with clearance_m = 0.5, which includes robot half width + margin? clearance_m is center clearance requested (0.5). segment_free uses need = _base_grid_clearance(clearance_m) = half width + max(0, clearance - half width) = 0.25 + (0.5-0.25)=0.5. So segment_free requires center clearance >=0.5. Our path may have cells where center clearance is just above 0.5 but actual robot width may be too close to walls? However map check uses margin = clearance -0.25 = 0.25 for check_path. So path should be okay.

But collisions with moving object (forklift) cannot be avoided by static map. The robot should slow down when object predicted to intersect. Our follow_cmd may produce high speed (v up to 1.5) even when distance to target is moderate (e.g., 2m). According to spec, v = min(1.5, 2.5*dist+0.5). For dist=2, v = min(1.5, 5+0.5)=1.5. That's max speed. Might be okay. However object prediction may not be enough; maybe our lookahead_target selects point far ahead (up to 2m) causing robot to travel at high speed through moving object. The chooser could still pick follow if object prediction says safe (maybe object speed low). But collisions happen with moving object (arena mover). Possibly the issue is that lookahead_target uses _base_loop_forward_target which respects target_max_ahead 2.0m, but does not respect target_path_limit_m (max distance from path) which is 1.0m. However forward_target uses robot projection based on path, so it's on path, okay.

But the root cause may be that our lookahead_target returns a point as (x,y) but base expects a tuple (x,y) that is used as target in guard. That's fine.

Maybe the failure is due to missing handling of case when _base_loop_forward_target returns None (no forward range). We fallback to path[-1] which is far; guard will then reject and fallback to forward_target again, but we already passed through guard after that, so maybe not.

The collisions are many (27) within short time (first collision at 31.433, simulation ends at 37.433). So after hitting moving object, simulation aborts after 5s. So after first collision, many collisions counted? maybe multiple contacts.

Thus primary failure is collision with dynamic object. The static planner cannot avoid moving object; need to adjust follow_cmd to be more conservative (reduce speed) to allow chooser to stop earlier? The chooser already checks object predictions with horizon 3s, but if speed high, predicted path may intersect. However our follow_cmd speed is high; chooser could still reject follow if collision predicted; but logs show follow was rarely chosen after t=26.5; after that only back, turn_r, forward_slow. So maybe follow was safe but moving object collided anyway because object prediction inaccurate (object speed high). The spec says object predictor may be inaccurate; we cannot modify base. But we can modify lookahead_target to keep target closer (shorter ahead) to reduce speed. The spec: lookahead target distance 0.3-2.0m. Our forward_target picks up to 2.0m, but may pick near max. If we limit to nearer, speed lower. So modify lookahead_target to cap ahead distance to e.g., 0.6m (just above min). That reduces speed and may avoid collisions.

Thus function to change: lookahead_target. Provide change: use _base_loop_forward_target but then clamp distance to 0.6m. We can compute point at 0.6m ahead along path from robot projection, using _base_loop_point_at_s.

Implementation: compute robot projection as before, then compute target_s = robot["s"] + 0.6 (or min max). Use _base_loop_point_at_s. Ensure segment_free from pose to target. If not, fallback to robot projection.
